newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya shilling hits official record low vs dlr.
newsitem.headline: Kenya shilling hits official record low vs dlr.

text.p: The Kenyan shilling declined to an official record low against the dollar on Thursday on sustained pressure from investors pulling out of the market.

The shilling was quoted at a commercial average of 70.2 against the dollar at 2 p.m. (1100 GMT) from 68.55 at 0730 GMT and a closing rate of 67.50 on Wednesday. The shilling decline against the dollar from Thursday was 4.0 percent.

The Central Bank of Kenya lists the all-time shilling-dollar low rate at 69.22 but commercial banks say a central bank instrument that put premium on the dollar in October 1993 meant real market rates reached 83.

Last Thursday, the International Monetary Fund (IMF) halted a $205 million three-year aid package under the soft-lending Enhanced Structural Adjustment Facility (ESAF) to Kenya in a row over corruption.

On Wednesday, Central Bank of Kenya Governor Micah Cheserem appealed to foreign exchange participants to trade "in an orderly manner so that losses arising from the panic and speculative transactions would be minimised."

Commercial dealers said on Wednesday investors were alarmed by President Daniel arap Moi playing down the IMF ruling and urging Kenyans to become self-reliant. He also said the lost IMF loans were insignificant compared to Kenya's whole economy.
